glosses: To perceive sounds through the ear.

examples.text: I was deaf, and now I can hear.

glosses: To perceive (a sound, or something producing a sound) with the ear, to recognize (something) in an auditory way.

examples.text: I could hear them quarreling upstairs, but didn’t really listen to their argument.

Mr. Cooke at once began a tirade against the residents of Asquith for permitting a sandy and generally disgraceful condition of the roads. So roundly did he vituperate the inn management in particular, and with such a loud flow of words, that I trembled lest he should be heard on the veranda.

glosses: To exercise this faculty intentionally; to listen to.

examples.text: Agayne there was dissencion amonge the iewes for these sayinges, and many of them sayd: He hath the devyll, and is madde: why heare ye hym?

glosses: To listen favourably to; to grant (a request etc.).

examples.text: Eventually the king chose to hear her entreaties.

glosses: To receive information about; to come to learn of.

examples.text: Adam, soon as he heard / The fatal Trespass don by Eve, amaz'd, / Astonied stood and Blank […]

She left and I never heard from her again.

glosses: To listen to (a person, case) in a court of law; to try.

examples.text: Your case will be heard at the end of the month.

glosses: To sympathize with; to understand the feelings or opinion of.

examples.text: You're tired of all the ads on TV? I hear ya.

examples.translation: 阿摩尼烏斯，同時是辛普里基烏斯與菲洛波努斯二人的老師，告訴我們，尤利安曾做出一項裁決 […] 以馬克西穆斯為優，因為馬克西穆斯曾受教於楊布里科斯，並追隨他與波菲利 (見《前分析篇注》31,15–22)。

examples.text: Charmadas, never actually Head of School but a prominent Academic who had himself heard Carneades, was prepared to teach Plato’s Gorgias […]
examples.translation: 卡爾馬達斯雖然從未真正擔任過學派之首，卻是一位舉足輕重的學園派學者，他本人曾受教於卡爾內阿德斯，並準備講授柏拉圖的《高爾吉亞篇》[…]
